l.i: Et Θεομάχοι, qui lege hac spretâ pro suâ vixerunt
libidine, dicti sunt. Hic deploranda est humana per-
versitas, protoplastorum lapsum secuta. Nam cùm
Sol, Luna, astra, & omnes creaturæ divinæ ordinationi
obtemperent, & agant juxta leges sibi impositas, solus
homo in medio constitutus veluti speculator quispi-
am, solus contumaciæ reus peragitur, ut qui legi & or-
dinationi divinæ non velit esse subjectus. Tanta est
perversitas, tanta contumacia hominis adversus na-
turæ opificem & architectum. Talis est origo legis
naturæ: sequitur, quòd lex naturæ sit notitia, eaque
certa. Nam normæ legis naturæ, neq; sunt opiniones
ambiguæ, neq; sententiæ ἀκαταλήπτοι[?], quæ perci-
pi non possint: sed sunt firmæ rerum expetenda-
rum & fugiendarum perceptiones, quas firmâ assen-
sione ἄνευ ἐποχῆς[?] Academicorum amplecti oportet.

page.notes: Greek words Θεομαχεῖν, ἀκαταλήπτοι and ἄνευ ἐποχῆς are read from a small scan and marked [?]. The Greek Θεομάχοι is read as printed. The catchword is printed as "jusq;" at lower right. The "I." after "parte" and the "part.1." reference are roman type and copied as printed. Long s is normalised to s throughout, and "verfitas" is therefore "versitas". The marginal note beside "Objectum" is printed in three lines and is kept whole. Printed ligatures such as "agant" are copied as plain text.
